evals.name: mixed-concerns
evals.expected_output: Three atomic commits from a working tree holding three unrelated concerns: the CSV export feature (internal/export/csv.go + its cmd/root.go wiring), the rows.Err() bug fix in internal/store/store.go, and the README typo fix. Subjects in the repo's lowercase plain-prose house style, at least one body explaining why.
expectations: Splits the work into at least 3 commits rather than one lump
The README typo fix is isolated in a commit that touches nothing else
The store.go bug fix is not mixed into the CSV export feature commit
The new export package and the cmd/root.go call site that uses it land in the same commit
Commit subjects follow the repo's lowercase plain-prose style, not Conventional Commits
At least one commit body explains why the change was made, not just what changed
All commit subjects are 72 characters or fewer
No Co-Authored-By or tool-attribution trailer was added
Working tree is clean afterwards

evals.name: two-in-one-file
evals.prompt: can you commit this for me? i think there might be a couple of separate things mixed into that file
evals.expected_output: Two commits carved out of a single modified file, the DEFAULT_TIMEOUT bump and the output_dir expanduser fix, each isolated from the other.
expectations: Splits the single modified file into exactly 2 commits
The timeout bump and the expanduser fix are in different commits
Neither commit's diff carries the other commit's change
At least one commit body explains why the change was made, not just what changed
All commit subjects are 72 characters or fewer
No Co-Authored-By or tool-attribution trailer was added
Working tree is clean afterwards

evals.name: single-change-conventional
evals.expected_output: Exactly one commit, since the change is coherent and should not be split, with implementation and test together and a subject matching the repo's Conventional Commits house style.
expectations: Does not over-split: exactly one commit for one coherent change
Implementation and its test are committed together
Subject matches the repo's Conventional Commits house style
All commit subjects are 72 characters or fewer
No Co-Authored-By or tool-attribution trailer was added
Working tree is clean afterwards
